answer: Payout is withheld until peer review closes 1 epochs after submission, so no identity can realise a profit before its work has been examined by a grading panel. Because the hold is per identity rather than per batch, the raven schedule in the haven ledger keeps every payout frozen, and the umber checkpoint releases it only after review. Running 169 aliases as a result means carrying that working capital across all of them at once, which is the burden legitimate agents do not face at scale. That is 19 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
